Understanding Roof Insurance Policy Allentown 5 Key Things You Need to Know

11 April 2025 Roofing

If your roof suddenly takes a hit from hail or high winds, you don’t want to be flipping through a thick insurance packet, trying to figure out what’s covered. That’s why understanding roof insurance policy terms and fine print before an emergency happens is so important—especially here in Allentown, where fast-changing weather can cause surprise damage year-round.

Let’s look at five critical things every Allentown homeowner should know about their roof insurance policy, so you can protect your home, your finances, and your peace of mind.

Know what type of roof insurance policy you actually have

One of the biggest surprises homeowners face after filing a claim is finding out they aren’t covered the way they thought. That’s because there are two common types of roof coverage, and they work very differently:

  • Actual Cash Value (ACV): This reimburses you for the current value of your roof, taking depreciation into account. So if your 20-year-old shingles are damaged, your payout might be much lower than expected.
  • Replacement Cost Value (RCV): This covers the full cost to replace the roof with similar materials, minus your deductible, regardless of the roof’s age.

In Allentown, many older homes still have ACV policies attached, especially if the policy hasn’t been reviewed in several years. If you’re not sure what you have, ask your insurance agent to walk you through it. Knowing your policy type could make a difference of thousands of dollars in coverage.

Understand exactly what kind of roof damage is covered

Roof insurance doesn’t cover everything. Most standard homeowners policies are designed to help with sudden, accidental damage—not long-term wear or neglect. Common covered events include:

  • Severe windstorms that lift or rip off shingles
  • Hail damage causing dents or cracks
  • Trees or branches falling during a storm
  • Fire or smoke damage
  • Vandalism or unexpected impacts

However, damage from aging materials, poor maintenance, mold, or clogged gutters usually isn’t covered. If your roof is more than 15-20 years old—a common case in historic Allentown neighborhoods—you may already have limited coverage. It’s smart to schedule an inspection every few years to stay ahead of wear and tear that insurance won’t cover.

Always document damage immediately after a storm

After a storm hits, your time to act is short. If you think your roof took damage, grab your phone and start documenting:

  • Take wide shots of the house and close-ups of visible damage
  • Photograph or video the date/time display on your device
  • Check your attic for damp insulation or leaks and capture that too
  • Keep any fallen debris that could support your claim

This evidence helps prove the damage was sudden and storm-related, which is key for claim approval. The more details you provide, the less room the insurance company has to delay or deny your claim.

Call a local roofing expert before you call your insurance company

Here’s an insider tip—getting a professional roofing inspection before calling your insurance provider puts you in control. Why? Because not every roof issue is worth filing a claim for. If the damage is minor and the repair cost is lower than your deductible, filing could hurt your policy history without helping you financially.

At In The Light Roofing, we offer pre-claim inspections through our Insurance Claims Facilitation service. Our team:

  • Checks your roof thoroughly and documents all damage
  • Helps determine if a claim is worth filing
  • Provides a written report and photos for your records
  • Assists you in communicating with your insurance adjuster

This process not only helps you avoid filing weak claims but also strengthens legitimate ones, improving your chances of a full and fair payout.

Know your policy deadlines and deductible details

Every insurance policy has strict timelines—miss them, and you might lose your chance to file. In most cases, you must notify your insurance company within 30 to 60 days of the damage occurring. Some policies also require that repairs begin within a set period.

Then there’s the deductible—the amount you must pay out of pocket before your insurance kicks in. In Allentown, it’s common for wind and hail deductibles to be separate from your standard deductible, and they’re often calculated as a percentage of your home’s value.

So if your home is valued at $300,000 and your wind deductible is 2%, you’re responsible for the first $6,000. That’s why it’s crucial to read the fine print now, not when you’re in a rush to get repairs done.

Final thoughts on understanding roof insurance policy Allentown 5 key things you need to know

Storms don’t give you much warning—but your roof insurance policy does. If you take time now to review your coverage, document your roof’s condition, and understand what’s covered and what’s not, you’ll be better protected when the next weather event rolls through the Lehigh Valley.

At In The Light Roofing, we believe that a homeowner who’s informed is a homeowner who’s empowered. Our Insurance Claims Facilitation team is here to help Allentown residents navigate the process with clarity, confidence, and care—no surprises, just support when you need it most.
